newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds up ahead of rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds up ahead of rate decision.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds and Makams closed higher in dull trading on Monday ahead of the Bank of Israel's interest rate announcement, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.08 pct at 103.13
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct at 102.28
Volume was low at 113 million shekels with most of the trading concentrated in the Makams and unlinked bonds.
After the close of trading the Bank of Israel said it was lowering its key lending rate for March by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 13.9 percent.
"The rate cut was in line with investors' forecasts. Bond prices were reflecting expectations of a reduction of 0.3 to 0.5 percentage point," said Roy Meir of Simodan brokerage house.
CPI-linked bonds closed almost unchanged as investors awaited the rate decision, said Yosi Weidelfeld of Eyal Securities.

"Inflation-linked bonds are becoming less attractive. Unlinked bonds offer yields of 14 percent while 1997 inflation is expected to remain at 7-8 percent. This yield is much higher than the 4.2 percent offered by CPI-linked bonds," Meir said.
Nevertheless, Meir said that for the near term he believed prices for inflation-linked bonds would remain stable. "Most of the demand will be concentrated in unlinked bonds and Makams," he said.
He noted that unlinked bonds were the only segment of the market to show a rise today.

Dollar-linked bonds closed lower following the rise of the shekel against the dollar. In the local forex market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3420 shekels against 3.3510 shekels on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
